scope: Proposition 4.2 (Attainment and uniform bounds) of the manuscript “A radial continuum phase transition with algebraic decay” (preprints/A-radial-continuum-phase-transition-with-algebraic-decay-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 228 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d53cafa68c322a07), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose the size conditions on t in Proposi- tion 2.3 hold, including ct > 4(A + 1). For every 0 < a ≤ 2(A + 1), TaQ(β, h) = max d≥0  hd − H(β, d) + βa 2 d2  . (4.2) The active shifts in (4.1) are exactly the maximizing densities in (4.2); in particular, they are nonnegative and form a nonempty compact set. On each compact D ⊂ Ω, they lie in a common interval [0, U], independently of φ and a. The constant U may also be chosen uniformly for all sufficiently large t. The function TaQ is finite and convex on Ω, and 0 ≤ TaQ − Q ≤ CDa on D. (4.3) Here CD can be chosen uniformly for sufficiently large t. For fixed t, the pressures Q and transforms TaQ have common bounds on compact subsets of Ω, and common local Lipschitz bounds, uniformly over the same family and masses.
